name: Honolulu / City and County of Honolulu

Downtown Honolulu.name: Downtown Honolulu
Downtown Honolulu.description: Financial-district and civic core around Aloha Tower with office-to-residential conversions and the densest 311 volume on the island.

Chinatown.name: Chinatown
Chinatown.description: Historic low-rise commercial enclave with renovation-heavy permitting, night-market density, and preservation overlays.

Kakaako.name: Kakaako
Kakaako.description: Ward Village / Our Kakaako high-rise spine turning former industrial blocks into the metro's densest residential pipeline.

Waikiki.name: Waikiki
Waikiki.description: Resort-corridor spine on Kalakaua with hotel renovation, timeshare conversion, and the island's highest short-stay pressure.

Diamond Head & Kahala.name: Diamond Head & Kahala
Diamond Head & Kahala.description: High-value coastal estate stock east of Waikiki dominated by renovation permits and strict shoreline setbacks.

Hawaii Kai.name: Hawaii Kai
Hawaii Kai.description: Marina-planned east-Oahu community with ADU and waterfront-renovation activity at the island's southeastern edge.

Kailua.name: Kailua
Kailua.description: Windward beach town with cottage-to-estate renovations and STR-driven small-lot pressure around Kailua Beach.

Kaneohe.name: Kaneohe
Kaneohe.description: Bayfront suburban grid under the Pali with steady single-family infill and military-adjacent rental demand.

Aiea & Pearl City.name: Aiea & Pearl City
Aiea & Pearl City.description: Pearl Harbor-adjacent mid-island suburbs with rail-station infill and aging post-war tract replacement.

Mililani.name: Mililani
Mililani.description: Master-planned central plateau community with townhome infill and renovation-led permitting on the H-2 corridor.

Wahiawa.name: Wahiawa
Wahiawa.description: Pineapple-town grid at the island's saddle with sparse permitting and Schofield Barracks-adjacent rental stock.

Kapolei.name: Kapolei
Kapolei.description: Second-city civic and commercial node with the island's largest new-construction pipeline west of downtown.

Ewa Beach.name: Ewa Beach
Ewa Beach.description: South-loeward tract and Hoakalei marina growth edge with high single-family permit velocity.

Waianae.name: Waianae
Waianae.description: Leeward coast townships with sparse, shoreline-constrained development and high 311 volume relative to permit activity.

Haleiwa & Waialua.name: Haleiwa & Waialua
Haleiwa & Waialua.description: North Shore surf-town commercial spine with STR-driven cottage renovations and agricultural-lot pressure.

Laie & Sunset.name: Laie & Sunset
Laie & Sunset.description: Windward-north coastal villages with limited new construction and seasonal STR occupancy around Sunset Beach and Laie.
